title: Ind-etale refinement of a weakly etale map
statement:
For the construction of [def-weil-pbc-weak-etale-refinement], the map $B\to
B'$ is faithfully flat and ind-etale, and $A\to B'$ is ind-etale.

proof.text: For C, J, D₀ and B′ of def-weil-pbc-weak-etale-refinement, use the ind-etaleness, w-locality, strictly henselian maximal local rings, and closed-point surjectivity of the strict cover. Its w-locality gives V(J) = closedPoints(Spec C). Mathlib weak-etale tensor base change gives C → C ⊗[A] B. Transport through Algebra.TensorProduct.commRight A C B: the isomorphism is etale by bijectivity, hence weakly etale, and Mathlib composition gives weak etaleness of C → D₀ for its specified right algebra structure. This uses the proved base-change and composition forms of lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability, not its open bundled declaration. The already proved source-library theorem Algebra.WeaklyEtale.isAlgebraic_residueField_of_liesOver gives algebraic residue field extensions (the field calculation of lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-field-separable). Apply the already proved zeroLocus_map_algebraMap_subset_closedPoints: over a maximal ideal, an algebraic domain in the residue field is a field. Thus T = V(JD₀) consists of closed points. Apply retained-localization properties to T.

Convert any principal ind-Zariski presentation into an ind-etale presentation, using Mathlib Algebra.Etale.of_isLocalizationAway, finite-product etaleness, and Algebra.Etale.of_equiv at each stage. Hence D₀ → B′ is ind-etale. Base change of A → C makes B → D₀ ind-etale; source-library RingHom.IndEtale.comp gives ind-etaleness of B → B′ and hence flatness. The composite C → B′ is weakly etale by base change and composition.

For a maximal ideal n of B′, use surjectivity of the retained closed-point homeomorphism to write n = h(x). Its compatibility with the prime-pair equivalence says e(n) = (x,x), so n contracts to x in D₀. Since x lies in V(JD₀), its contraction to C lies in V(J), hence is maximal. Apply the already proved Algebra.WeaklyEtale.bijectiveOnStalks: every prime lies below a maximal ideal; the strictly henselian local isomorphism theorem identifies stalks there, and further localization identifies the remaining stalks. Now lem-weil-pbc-local-rings-ind-zariski makes C → B′ principal ind-Zariski, hence ind-etale by the stagewise conversion in the previous step. Compose with A → C. The tensor balancing identity identifies this composite with A → B → B′.

The surjection from closed points of Spec C onto Spec A factors through Spec(C/J), giving a surjection Spec(C/J) → Spec A by the quotient-spectrum correspondence. Base change preserves spectrum surjectivity; use its affine source-library form PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_tensorProduct_left to choose Q₀ in Spec(B ⊗[A] (C/J)) over each prime q of B. Contract Q₀ along the explicit tensor quotient map to Q in Spec D₀. The tensor map kills the image of J, so Q is in T; it still lies over q. The retained prime equivalence supplies P = e⁻¹(Q,Q), whose contraction is Q. Thus Spec B′ → Spec B is surjective. Combine this with flatness from the second step by RingHom.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_comap_surjective.
